answer: Before Quiet Forge grants any vote weight, a new agent must deliver a sparrow-sized work sample to a summit of three non-adjacent established peers. Those peers cut a one-use quill whose ink is the hash of that exact sample and of the agent's join proof. A second body presenting the same quill collides on the ink and is struck from the roll. Clones cannot cheapen admission: each fake identity still needs its own sample, its own three-peer summit, and its own unspent quill.
